about: Names, descriptions and grades are the official PlayStation 5 list as published by Exophase and PSNProfiles. Guides and steps are written for the Leonida Trophy Atlas from those official descriptions; every guide cites its sources. Hidden flags follow PlayStation's published count of 28 hidden trophies, assigned to the story-linked ones. Missable flags are reasoned from the descriptions: a trophy is flagged when its description ties it to a one-time story beat, a choice, a partner, or a character strand that can close as chapters advance.

trophies.name: Vice Got a Price!
trophies.guide: The platinum, earned the moment the other 54 trophies are yours. There is nothing to do for this one directly: work the roadmap stops in order — story, strands, activities, collectibles, crime — and it lands with the last trophy of the set.
steps: Follow the six roadmap stops in this atlas; the platinum is Stop 6.
Clear the 19 missable trophies during the story and strands (Stops 1–2) so no second playthrough is needed.
Finish with the 100% sweep (A Long Road); the platinum follows the final trophy automatically.

trophies.name: Just Like Paradise
trophies.guide: The opening mission trophy: finish Gone Fishing, the first story mission. It cannot be missed — the campaign starts here, and the trophy pops as the mission ends.
steps: Start the story and play the opening mission, Gone Fishing, to its end.
No special conditions: completion alone earns it.

sources.label: GTA Wiki — Grand Theft Auto VI

trophies.name: Paradise Lost
trophies.guide: Finish every mission in Chapter 1. Chapter trophies in this series are pure progression markers, so simply play the story forward; if a side strand opens during the chapter, clear it before moving on (see Stop 2).
steps: Play Chapter 1's missions in order until the chapter closes.
Before the chapter's final mission, check the map for open strands and finish them.

sources.label: GTA Wiki — Grand Theft Auto VI

trophies.name: T**s Ass Drug Money
trophies.guide: Finish Chapter 2. Same rule as every chapter trophy: story progression only, nothing to fail. The name is PlayStation's own, asterisks and all.
steps: Complete Chapter 2's missions until the chapter ends.
Sweep any strands that opened during the chapter before its finale.

trophies.name: Vice City, Baby!
trophies.guide: Finish Chapter 3. By now the map should be opening up; keep the habit of clearing strands and one-time moments (the missable flags in this atlas) before each chapter finale.
steps: Complete Chapter 3's missions in order.
Check this atlas's Missables view before the chapter's last mission.

sources.label: GTA Wiki — Grand Theft Auto VI

trophies.name: Top Of The World, Ma
trophies.guide: Finish Chapter 4, the last numbered chapter before the finale. After this the story runs to its final mission, so anything strand-shaped still open should be finished now.
steps: Complete Chapter 4's missions.
Before the finale, clear every open character strand (Stop 2).

sources.label: GTA Wiki — Grand Theft Auto VI

trophies.name: You Gotta Know When to Get Off
trophies.guide: The story's gold: complete the final mission. It is unmissable, but treat the point of no return with respect — finish strands, partner trophies and one-time moments first, because the world after the credits may not offer them the same way.
steps: Before starting the final mission, clear Stop 2 strands and the partner trophies (Hot Together, Retail Therapy).
Play the final mission to the credits; the gold pops at completion.

trophies.name: Trust
trophies.guide: Complete the named story mission Breakfast Run. Named-mission trophies pop on completion regardless of how the mission went, so no medal or condition is needed.
steps: Reach Breakfast Run in the story and finish it.
Completion alone earns the trophy.

sources.label: GTA Wiki — Grand Theft Auto VI

trophies.name: Break the Bank
trophies.guide: Complete The Cartel Heist, a named story mission. Heists in this series often carry choices; the trophy only asks for completion, but note that choice-driven progress (Actions Speak Louder) also accrues here.
steps: Play The Cartel Heist when the story offers it and see it through.
Any approach counts; the trophy is for completion.

sources.label: GTA Wiki — Grand Theft Auto VI

trophies.name: Family Matters
trophies.guide: Complete the named story mission Child's Play. A straight completion trophy on the main path.
steps: Reach Child's Play in the story and finish it.
No extra conditions apply.

sources.label: GTA Wiki — Grand Theft Auto VI

trophies.name: DWNFALL
trophies.guide: Complete the named story mission Headliners. Main-path progression; it cannot be skipped or failed permanently.
steps: Play Headliners when it unlocks and complete it.
Completion alone earns the trophy.

sources.label: GTA Wiki — Grand Theft Auto VI

trophies.name: Hi-Jacked
trophies.guide: Complete VCIA Takedown, the named mission at Vice City International Airport. Watch this mission closely: Catch Me If You Can (an unscheduled departure at VCIA) is tied to the same place and is flagged missable in this atlas, so save before it.
steps: Make a manual save before starting VCIA Takedown.
Complete the mission; then check whether Catch Me If You Can also popped — if not, reload and look for the unscheduled departure.

sources.label: GTA Wiki — Grand Theft Auto VI

trophies.name: Snow Storm
trophies.guide: Complete Operation Savage Glory, a named story mission. Straight progression, earned at the mission's end.
steps: Reach Operation Savage Glory in the story and finish it.
No side conditions are named in the description.

sources.label: GTA Wiki — Grand Theft Auto VI

trophies.name: A Long Road
trophies.guide: Reach 100% completion — the second gold, and the long pole of the platinum. In this series 100% means the story plus the tracked side content: strands, activities, collectibles, properties and challenges. Work Stops 1–5 of the roadmap and use the in-game completion checklist to find the last stragglers; this atlas's counters mirror the same totals.
steps: Finish the story (Stop 1) and every strand (Stop 2).
Clear activities, collectibles and crime (Stops 3–5) using the counters on each trophy card.
Open the in-game completion screen and chase whatever category is short; the gold pops at 100%.

trophies.name: Cunning Stunts
trophies.guide: Complete 250 stunts — the silver for the series' stunt jumps and stunt challenges. The description gives the count only, so treat every marked jump and stunt spot as progress: work them district by district during free roam and let the counter on this card track the total.
steps: Unlock free roam, then hunt stunt jumps and stunt challenges area by area.
Repeat reliable jumps while travelling between other collectibles — every completion counts.
Track the total with the counter here; the silver pops at 250.

trophies.name: Master of None
trophies.description: Try each type of activity once.
trophies.guide: Try each of the 9 activity types at least once — a sampler trophy. The official list's tracked count is 9, and the other activity trophies name most of the menu: races, drone races, the shooting range, fishing, arcade games, bowling, stunts and challenges among them. One attempt at each is enough; winning is not required here.
steps: As each activity unlocks, play it once — win or lose, it registers.
Use the other activity trophies in Stop 3 as your checklist of types to sample.
The bronze pops when the ninth distinct type has been tried.

trophies.name: The Shootist
trophies.description: Earn a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges.
trophies.guide: Earn gold in all 42 Shooting Range challenges — the silver the official list counts to 42. Ranges in this series grade by score and time, so treat each lane as a short score attack: learn the target order, then run it until the gold threshold falls. Nothing here is missable; the range stays open in free roam.
steps: Find a Shooting Range once free roam opens and work through its challenge list.
For each challenge, run it repeatedly until the medal reads gold — accuracy first, speed second.
Use the counter here to track golds; all 42 earn the silver.

trophies.name: Top Fun
trophies.description: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every location.
trophies.guide: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at each of the 14 locations. One win per location is the whole requirement — find a Top Fun start point, learn its course, and take first place before moving to the next.
steps: Unlock Top Fun drone races in free roam.
Visit each of the 14 locations and win its race once.
Count wins on this card; 14 location wins earn the bronze.

sources.label: GTA Wiki — Grand Theft Auto VI

trophies.name: Earn Cash, Not Kudos
trophies.guide: Win 20 different races — distinct events, not the same race farmed twenty times. Street and circuit races across Leonida all count toward the twenty; vary the route each time and the trophy follows.
steps: Enter races as they appear on the map during free roam.
Win each event once, then move on — repeats do not add to the 20.
Track distinct wins with the counter here.

trophies.name: Baited My Tackle
trophies.description: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge.
trophies.missableWhy: Cal is a named character, so the challenge sits inside his strand. Strands in this series can close as chapters advance — beat Cal while his strand is still open rather than after the story ends.
trophies.guide: Beat Cal in his fishing challenge. The description names a person, not a place, which puts this inside Cal's strand: meet him, take the challenge when offered, and out-fish him. Do it during Stop 2, while the strand is live.
steps: Find Cal's strand during the story and accept his fishing challenge.
Beat his catch to win the challenge; retry while the strand stays open if he wins.
Finish before advancing the story past his strand.

sources.label: GTA Wiki — Grand Theft Auto VI

trophies.name: Stick Fiddler
trophies.guide: Complete any one arcade game. Arcades are free-roam fixtures in this series, so walk up to a cabinet, play to the end of a game, and the bronze is yours. It also ticks one of the nine activity types for Master of None.
steps: Find an arcade cabinet in free roam.
Play one game through to completion (a game over screen counts as completing the session).
The trophy pops when the game ends.

trophies.name: Road to Rehabilitation
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Andy.
trophies.missableWhy: Andy's strand ends with a final mission; if the story moves past the point where Andy is available, the strand — and this trophy — can close unfinished. Clear it during Stop 2.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission of Andy's strand. Work his missions as they appear on the map and keep going until the strand's last mission is done; the trophy pops at its end.
steps: Take Andy's missions whenever they are offered.
Continue the strand to its final mission before pushing the main story to its finale.
Completion of that last mission earns the bronze.

sources.label: GTA Wiki — Grand Theft Auto VI

trophies.name: This Was No Boat Accident
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Kenton.
trophies.missableWhy: Kenton's strand has a final mission that can be left behind if the story advances past him. Finish the strand while it is open (Stop 2).
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission of Kenton's strand. Follow his missions to the end of the chain; the trophy is for the last one, not the first.
steps: Play Kenton's missions as they unlock.
Keep returning until the strand's final mission appears, then complete it.
Do this before the story's final mission.

sources.label: GTA Wiki — Grand Theft Auto VI

trophies.name: The Lone Rider
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Billy.
trophies.missableWhy: Billy's final mission sits at the end of his strand; strands can close when chapters advance, so finish Billy's chain during Stop 2 instead of after the credits.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission of Billy's strand. Ride the whole chain out — the trophy waits at the end of it.
steps: Take Billy's missions as they appear.
Continue until the final mission of the strand and complete it.
Clear it before the story finale.

sources.label: GTA Wiki — Grand Theft Auto VI

trophies.name: Strangers & Freaks
trophies.description: Complete 8 mission strands for strangers across the state of Leonida.
trophies.missableWhy: Stranger strands are the classic missable content in this series: givers move on as the story advances. Eight completed strands are needed, so finish strangers as you meet them rather than banking them for the endgame.
trophies.guide: Complete 8 mission strands for strangers across Leonida — the silver for the state's oddballs. A strand counts when its whole chain is finished, so when a stranger appears on the map, see their story through instead of taking one mission and leaving.
steps: Whenever a stranger strand opens, play it to its final mission.
Spread across the state: strands are Leonida-wide, so explore between chapters.
Count completed strands here; eight earn the silver.

sources.label: GTA Wiki — Strangers and Freaks (series conventions)

trophies.name: Supply & Demand
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Randy.
trophies.missableWhy: Randy's strand ends in a final mission that the story can move past. Finish the chain while it is open (Stop 2).
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission of Randy's strand. As with every strand trophy here, only the last mission counts — keep taking Randy's work until the chain ends.
steps: Play Randy's missions as they unlock.
Return for each follow-up until the final mission, then complete it.
Clear the strand before the story's final mission.

sources.label: GTA Wiki — Grand Theft Auto VI

trophies.name: Spin On This!
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Tyrone.
trophies.missableWhy: Tyrone's final mission closes his strand; leave the strand unfinished while chapters advance and it can close without you. Finish it during Stop 2.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission of Tyrone's strand. Work the chain from first job to last; the bronze is waiting at the end of it.
steps: Take Tyrone's missions whenever they are offered.
Continue to the strand's final mission and complete it.
Do it before the story finale.

sources.label: GTA Wiki — Grand Theft Auto VI

trophies.name: Positive Mental Attitude
trophies.description: Meditate at every spot across Leonida.
trophies.guide: Meditate at all 18 spots across Leonida. A pure collectible sweep: the spots are fixed points in the world, so tour them district by district during Stop 4 and tick each one off here as you sit down at it.
steps: In free roam, travel to each meditation spot and meditate.
Work one district at a time so no spot is visited twice or skipped.
All 18 spots earn the bronze.

trophies.name: Fair Game
trophies.description: Hunt a unique animal for Bret.
trophies.missableWhy: The hunt is for Bret, a named character, which puts it inside his strand. Strands can close as the story advances — take Bret's hunt while his strand is open (Stop 2), even though the hunting itself is a collectible-style sweep.
trophies.guide: Hunt a unique animal for Bret. Meet Bret, take his hunting job, and track down the one-of-a-kind animal he wants. Because it is tied to a character, treat it as strand content and do it while Bret is still around.
steps: Find Bret's strand and accept his hunting request.
Track and hunt the unique animal he names.
Complete it before advancing the story past Bret.

trophies.name: Don't Touch My Deck
trophies.guide: Complete 3 collectible card sets — the silver for the card hunt. Cards are scattered collectibles; finishing a set means finding every card in it. Sweep district by district in Stop 4 and check the in-game collection screen to see which cards each set still needs.
steps: Collect cards as you explore; open the collection screen to see set progress.
Focus one set at a time until it is complete, then move to the next.
Three completed sets earn the silver.

trophies.name: You WAiNKer!
trophies.guide: WAiNK It at 100 locations — the silver for Leonida's hundred WAiNK spots. Like every collectible sweep here, the efficient route is geographic: clear one district's spots before moving on, and let the counter on this card keep the running total.
steps: In free roam, visit WAiNK spots and use them as you find them.
Sweep district by district to avoid backtracking.
The silver pops at the 100th location.

trophies.name: One Last Thing
trophies.guide: Complete 50 challenges. Challenges are the game's tracked side-goals; they complete as you play activities, drive, fight and explore. Keep an eye on the challenge list, pick the ones close to done, and finish them off — fifty completions earn the bronze.
steps: Open the challenges list in free roam and note which are nearly complete.
Finish challenges opportunistically while doing Stops 3–5.
Track the total here; 50 completions earn the trophy.

trophies.name: Hot Together
trophies.description: Lose a 4 star Wanted Level with your partner and escape the heat.
trophies.missableWhy: It needs your partner beside you. Partner availability is story-driven, so earn this while the partnership is active — ideally before the final mission — rather than assuming your partner will still ride along after the credits.
trophies.guide: Lose a 4-star Wanted Level with your partner and escape the heat. Raise the heat to four stars with your partner in tow, then break line of sight and stay hidden until the stars clear. The partner requirement is the catch: do it while the story still has you riding together.
steps: With your partner with you, cause enough chaos to reach a 4-star Wanted Level.
Break police line of sight and hide until the wanted level fully clears.
The trophy pops when the heat is gone and you are both still free.

trophies.name: Retail Therapy
trophies.description: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner without losing your Wanted Level.
trophies.missableWhy: Three robberies back-to-back with your partner, wanted level intact throughout. It needs your partner present, so do it while the partnership is active — before the final mission is safest.
trophies.guide: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner without ever losing your Wanted Level. Plan a short route of three nearby shops: rob the first to raise the heat, then hit the second and third while the stars are still up. If the wanted level clears between shops, start the run over.
steps: Pick three shops close together and bring your partner.
Rob shop one; keep the wanted level alive while moving to shop two, then shop three.
The third robbery with the heat still on earns the bronze.

trophies.name: Whip It Good
trophies.guide: Discover 100 vehicles. Discovery in this series means encountering and getting into distinct vehicle models; variety is the point. Hop into anything new you see while exploring — the counter here tracks distinct discoveries toward 100.
steps: Enter every new vehicle model you come across in free roam.
Check car meets, parking areas and traffic in each district for models you have not tried.
The bronze pops at the 100th distinct vehicle.

trophies.name: Gunslinger
trophies.description: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus.
trophies.guide: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus. Set it up where enemies cluster — a gang operation or a heated mission fight — then trigger Combat Focus and drop five before it ends. Repeatable anywhere, so retry freely.
steps: Find a fight with at least five enemies close together.
Trigger Combat Focus and take down five enemies before it expires.
If it falls short, refill and try the next cluster.

trophies.name: Catch Me If You Can
trophies.description: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA.
trophies.missableWhy: VCIA is the airport from the story mission VCIA Takedown (Hi-Jacked). An 'unscheduled departure' reads as a one-time moment inside that mission's window — save before the mission and look for the departure while you are there.
trophies.guide: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA — Vice City International Airport, the setting of the story mission VCIA Takedown. The wording points at a specific escape moment during that mission rather than free-roam flying, so keep a save before the mission and watch for the chance to leave the airport your own way.
steps: Save manually before starting VCIA Takedown.
During the mission, look for the unscheduled way out of VCIA and take it.
If the mission ends without the trophy, reload the save and try the other exit.

sources.label: GTA Wiki — Grand Theft Auto VI

trophies.name: Challenging Tank
trophies.missableWhy: Rhinos are tanks, and 'kinda hot in these Rhinos' reads as a scripted story moment rather than a free-roam activity. Flagged missable: when the story puts you in or against a Rhino, see the moment through instead of skipping past it.
trophies.guide: Kinda hot in these Rhinos — a moment trophy tied to the Rhino tank. The description is a quote, which in this series usually marks a specific story beat. When the campaign puts a Rhino in front of you, play the beat out; if a choice is offered, take the one that keeps you in the tank.
steps: Keep a save before missions that mention military hardware.
When a Rhino appears in the story, complete the sequence involving it.
If the moment passes without the trophy, reload and replay the beat.

trophies.name: Sneakthief
trophies.description: Rob a jewelry store without being detected.
trophies.guide: Rob a jewelry store without being detected. Case the store first: get in, take what you came for, and get out unseen — no wanted level, no witnesses raising the alarm. If you are spotted, leave and try again another night; robberies reset.
steps: Pick a jewelry store and approach when it is quiet.
Rob it while staying undetected — avoid cameras and witnesses where you can.
Leave clean; the bronze pops when the robbery completes unseen.

trophies.name: Maximum Withdrawal
trophies.guide: Rob 5 bank vaults and escape — the silver for Leonida's vaults. Each vault job needs both halves: crack the vault, then lose the heat and get away clean. Five successful escapes earn it; a failed escape does not count, so plan the getaway before you go in.
steps: Case a bank vault and plan an escape route and a fast vehicle.
Rob the vault, then escape until the wanted level clears.
Repeat at five vaults; track escapes on this card.

trophies.name: A Classic Blitz Play
trophies.description: Rob an Armored Truck and escape.
trophies.guide: Rob an armored truck and escape. Spot one on its route, stop it, take the cash, and lose the heat. The escape is part of the trophy — the bronze pops once you are clear, not when the doors open.
steps: Find an armored truck in free roam and block or ram it to a stop.
Rob it, then break line of sight and lose the wanted level.
One clean escape earns the trophy.

trophies.name: The Goodtime State
trophies.guide: Explore all of Leonida — every one of its 52 areas. Exploration trophies in this series tick off as you enter each named area, so a grand tour by road, boat and air does the job. Pair it with the collectible sweeps in Stop 4 and the map fills itself in.
steps: Travel through every district and island of Leonida.
Watch the area name pop as you cross borders; use the map to find greyed-out gaps.
The bronze pops when the 52nd area registers.

trophies.name: Pest Control
trophies.description: Rob an Illegal Operation belonging to each gang.
trophies.guide: Rob an illegal operation belonging to each of the 9 gangs. One operation per gang is the whole ask: find each gang's racket, hit it, and move on. Work gang by gang so you never rob the same crew twice by mistake.
steps: Identify each gang's illegal operation as you explore Leonida.
Rob one operation per gang — nine gangs, nine robberies.
Track gangs done on this card; the ninth earns the bronze.

trophies.name: In The Beginning…
trophies.description: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach.
trophies.missableWhy: The name says it: 'In The Beginning…' points at an early-game moment on Ocean Beach. One-time scene trophies like this usually sit inside an early mission — take the cocktail when the story offers it instead of rushing past.
trophies.guide: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach. The trophy's name frames it as an opening-hours moment, so when the early story puts you on Ocean Beach with a drink in reach, stop and take in the view. If it is offered as an interaction, use it before moving on.
steps: Early in the story, when you reach Ocean Beach, look for the cocktail spot with a view.
Use the interaction and let the moment play out.
If you pass it by, reload an early save — it may not come back.

sources.label: GTA Wiki — Grand Theft Auto VI

trophies.name: Capital Offense
trophies.description: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style.
trophies.missableWhy: 'In classic style' marks a scripted set-piece: a showroom breakout the story stages once. Flagged missable — when the campaign puts you in a vehicle showroom, drive out through the glass instead of taking a quiet exit.
trophies.guide: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style. This reads as a staged story moment: a showroom, a car, and a plate-glass exit. When the mission puts you there, floor it through the window rather than slipping out the back.
steps: Keep a save before showroom-set missions.
When the moment comes, drive out through the showroom glass.
If the scene ends without the trophy, reload and take the loud exit.

sources.label: GTA Wiki — Grand Theft Auto VI

trophies.name: Let’s Go Bowling
trophies.description: Follow-through at the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley.
trophies.missableWhy: It names one specific alley — Kolt & Associates' — which ties it to a strand or a scripted visit rather than any bowling lane. Flagged missable: bowl there when the story or a strand takes you, and do not assume the alley stays open forever.
trophies.guide: Follow-through at the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley: play bowling at that named alley. Because the description pins a specific business, treat it as strand content — when you are sent there (or find it open), bowl a game and finish it.
steps: Find the Kolt & Associates bowling alley during the story or its strand.
Play a game of bowling there through to the end.
Do it while the alley is reachable; do not leave it for after the credits.

trophies.name: Personal Best
trophies.missableWhy: 'A partnership with mass appeal' is a quoted moment about the partnership at the heart of the story — a one-time scene, not a repeatable activity. Flagged missable: let partnership scenes play out fully instead of skipping ahead.
trophies.guide: A partnership with mass appeal — a story-moment trophy about the central partnership. Quote-style descriptions in this list mark specific scenes, so when the story stages a public moment for the pair, see it through to the end of the scene.
steps: Play partnership-focused story missions without skipping their scenes.
When a public, crowd-facing moment arrives, let it finish.
Keep a save before major partnership missions in case the moment is choice-gated.

trophies.name: Actions Speak Louder
trophies.missableWhy: PlayStation tracks a count to 500 for this one, and the description is about choices. Choices are finite per playthrough, so engage with every choice the story and strands offer instead of rushing past them — a playthrough that skips optional content may fall short of 500.
trophies.guide: Choices made (for better or worse) — PlayStation tracks this one to a count of 500. Every decision the game puts in front of you counts: story branches, strand outcomes, how you handle encounters. The safe route is to play everything — full story, all strands, optional interactions — and let the counter climb naturally.
steps: Take every choice the story and strands present; do not skip optional content.
Play all of Stop 2's strands — each adds decisions to the count.
Check the tracked count as you go; 500 choices earn the bronze.

trophies.name: Bad Luck, I Guess
trophies.missableWhy: 'Second time's the charm' implies a fail-then-succeed beat: something must go wrong once before it can go right. Scripted two-attempt moments are one-time story content, so flagged missable — when a scene offers a retry, take it rather than reloading to a perfect first try.
trophies.guide: Second time's the charm: succeed at something on the second attempt after the first goes wrong. When a story beat or activity lets you fail and immediately retry, take the retry and succeed — the trophy is about the comeback, not a flawless first run.
steps: When a mission or challenge fails and offers an immediate retry, accept it.
Succeed on that second attempt.
Do not reload to erase the failure first — the failed attempt is part of the trophy.

sources.label: GTA Wiki — Grand Theft Auto VI

trophies.name: The Truth Is Out There
trophies.missableWhy: 'What the hell just happened?' marks a strange one-time encounter — the series loves a single weird event hidden in the world. Flagged missable: when something inexplicable happens, stay and witness it instead of driving on.
trophies.guide: What the hell just happened? — witness something strange. Every game in this series hides at least one inexplicable encounter in the world. Explore off the beaten path, and when the game shows you something that makes no sense, stop and watch it finish.
steps: Explore remote corners of Leonida between missions.
When a strange event triggers, stay and let it play out.
The bronze pops once you have witnessed it.

trophies.name: Ten Pin
trophies.description: Bowl 'em over with a melee drive-by.
trophies.guide: Bowl 'em over with a melee drive-by: knock someone down with a melee attack from a moving vehicle. Cruise past a target at low speed, swing as you pass, and connect. Repeatable anywhere in free roam — a quiet street and a slow roll make it easy.
steps: Get in a vehicle and find a pedestrian or enemy near the road.
Drive past slowly and land a melee drive-by hit that knocks them down.
One clean knockdown earns the bronze.

trophies.name: Dime on the Dollar
trophies.description: Earn $250,000 laundering Marked Bills through your contacts.
trophies.guide: Earn $250,000 laundering Marked Bills through your contacts. Robberies and heists pay in marked bills; your contacts wash them into clean money at a cut. Keep feeding bills through your contacts after every score in Stop 5 and the quarter-million arrives on its own.
steps: Earn Marked Bills from robberies and heists.
Launder them through your contacts whenever you are carrying a stack.
Track the laundered total here; $250,000 earns the bronze.

trophies.name: Treat Yo Self
trophies.guide: Spend $100,000 across all shops. Weapons, clothes, vehicle work — every till in Leonida counts toward the same total. By the time Stop 5's crime money is laundered, a shopping spree finishes this quickly.
steps: Buy gear, outfits and vehicle upgrades as you play; every purchase counts.
After big scores, spend deliberately at shops across the map.
$100,000 in total spending earns the bronze.

trophies.name: Little Boxes
trophies.guide: Purchase all 8 garage properties. Properties come up for sale as the story and your wallet grow; buy each garage when it is offered. Eight purchases — one per property — earn the bronze, and the garages double as storage for the vehicle hunts.
steps: Check property listings as new areas open up.
Buy each garage property when you can afford it.
All 8 owned earns the trophy.

trophies.name: On the Spot
trophies.description: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app.
trophies.guide: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app. Whenever you get a vehicle worth keeping, register it in the app; ten registrations finish the trophy. It pairs naturally with Whip It Good's hundred discoveries — register the keepers as you find them.
steps: Open the Scooter Bros app when you have a vehicle you like.
Register it; repeat with nine more distinct vehicles.
The tenth registration earns the bronze.
